english.title: Fail to provide specimen - person in charge of vehicle
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) when suspected of having been in charge of a vehicle and having been required to provide

(A)_[a specimen or specimens of breath for analysis by means of a device of a type approved by the Secretary of State]_
(B)_[a specimen of blood for a laboratory test]_
(C)_[a specimen of urine for a laboratory test]_

pursuant to section 7 of the Road Traffic Act 1988 in the course of an investigation into whether you had committed an offence under section 3A, 4, 5 or 5A thereof, failed, without reasonable excuse, to do so
english.legislation: Contrary to section 7(6) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence wording follows the house of lords ruling in DPP v Butterworth . 21.9.94
(ii) See also associated offence wordings as follows: H29.
(iii) Specified Drug Limits for the purpose of section 5A of the Road Traffic Act 1988 have only been set in blood. As such, in relation to section 5A, an officer may make a requirement for blood only. Where a driver is unable to provide a blood specimen an officer may make a requirement for urine only where impairment (under section 4) is also being investigated.
